channel.title: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?" - Want to help shape the future of the site?

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
As a general note, the Butterfly Squad is the only group of reviewers who handles critique of material before it is posted to the mainsite, and they review drafts and concepts, not just the latter.

Butterfly Squad is typically invitation-only, though I will take requests for consideration to join the Roster. Simply send me a PM noting you are interested in being considered—I will then respond with the criteria (generally links to recent reviews, and some statements about different aspects of the forum experience) to provide for staff to look over and determine if the reviewer should be added to the Roster.

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
is it still alright to leave unsolicited crit on threads we find interesting,

Totally alright! Encouraged, even. The best case scenario we're aiming for is reviewers enjoying the critique process by finding material that they are enthusiastic about critiquing.

is the idea to ensure that prospective authors are taking the initiative to find someone on their own?

Sort of. The main concern to address was that a lot of feedback simply went effectively ignored, as authors either did not respond to reviewers entirely or immediately dropped a concept after receiving a review that noted changes needed to be made.

By asking authors to take the initiative to reach out, the intention is to establish that the author is a. active and likely to reply to a reviewer and b. willing and able to put in more than just the bare minimum effort to get a concept review.

item.title: Re: Getting feedback
item.content:encoded:
So, what if your feedback was vague and unhelpful, yet you could still use some review on an idea. As, you can’t post multiple threads for one idea meaning the SCP really only has one shot in the idea section.

Presuming that you mean that the feedback you received was vague, and not the feedback you yourself gave was vague, you can and should reach out to reviewers.

If you're having trouble getting further replies on a thread, you can go to the IRC chatroom and ask people there if they can reply to the forum thread, or message a staff member and ask them if they can direct chat attention to the thread. You can also reach out to a reviewer on the Butterfly Squad Roster.

Also, does someone have to request a sandbox draft or can you add a link to one in your idea critique out of your own choice?

If you want to preemptively link a sandbox draft, it has to be optional reading only. Reviewers should not need to read a full draft to understand and discuss the core concept of a piece. An author should be prepared to answer reviewer questions directly, rather than needing to default to asking a reviewer to dig through a full draft for the answers.

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
As the saying goes, "Everyone's a critic."

You can critique on any thread you want so as long as your critique is of high quality. High quality being: Helpful feedback that isn't vague and that it addresses flaws and strong points of an idea. Additionally, also telling if the idea is a common trope and has a pitfall.

Basically, no. There's no such thing as "needing to be critter" to provide critique.

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
Does a reviewer need to be a successful author?

Not at all! The chef/food metaphor applies here: while chefs are more likely to give good advice on how to improve food, one doesn't necessarily need to be a chef to comment on whether food tastes good and what can be done to improve a dish (to their taste, at least).

Despite not being a successful author, I wish to be a reviewer.

Excellent! We could always use more talented reviewers on the site.

We do have a number of critique resources available in the Guide Hub, so feel free to reference the writing guides as you get started writing reviews in the forums.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Does a reviewer need to be a successful author? Or can anyone provide critique assuming they are well written and constructive with their criticism?

Yes, anyone can provide critique as long as they give constructive criticism (save for people given a cease and desist due to previous problematic critiques). The ability to greenlight however has more standards.

I would suggest however that you take some time to read how other people critique before doing it yourself (The butterfly squad roster is a great place to start. It hosts many experienced members of the forum). Many people need examples of constructive criticism to understand what makes it good.

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
Noting that per the new Draft Forum policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies

Before they can ask for forum feedback on a draft, first-time authors will need to get their concepts "greenlighted", either in the forums or IRC chatrooms, by two experienced reviewers from these lists:

  • Butterfly Squad Roster
  • Authors' Pages (or someone who meets the requirements for an author page)
  • Reviewers' Spotlight Archive
  • Meet The Staff

Put simply, a reviewer has "greenlighted" a concept if they state straightforwardly (or when prompted) that they believe a draft of the premise would be successful on the mainsite, and/or that they think the author should progress to the drafting stage.

item.title: Re: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
Typically joining the team is invitation-only, but we are always welcome to people requesting to be considered for a team position.

The best way to be noticed is to provide high-quality critique at a relatively consistent activity rate. Butterfly Squad members are expected to be both good reviewers and active reviewers.

ETA: updating with some information, as it was brought to my attention that this comment is somewhat out of date.

Staff will occasionally reach out to consistently active quality reviewers to extend invitations to have their name put on the Roster. Staff will also happily take requests for consideration to join the team, whenever a reviewer wishes to put their name forth as someone whom authors can contact to seek feedback from. Any further questions or clarifications about this can be directed to me (Zyn) via wikidot PM.

item.title: SO YOU WANT TO BE A CONCEPT REVIEWER?
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the Ideas Critique Forum!

This is where newbies and veterans alike come to shop their concepts around until they have something that they're ready to write into a full draft (or use to revamp an existing draft). This is where reviewers come into play, since we have a lot of widely read community members who remember thousands of SCPs!

If you'd like to help authors polish up their ideas and potentially think up the Next Best Thing, here are a few things to keep in mind!

1. Tell the author what you liked (or didn't like) about their idea, and why.

2. Tell the author what you think they should fix or do next, and why.

That's pretty much it!

Click to show some more detailed instructions
hide
  • Give the author a direction to follow!
    • Just saying "needs work"/"needs more"/"has potential" and leaving it at that is vague and unhelpful because the author doesn't know what specifically needs work or has potential.
    • Just saying "I like this a lot" / "I don't like this" is also too vague. What specific parts were good and can be kept after edits? What parts are weaker and can be trimmed?
  • Make sure you know what the community wants!
    • SCPs don't need to be dangerous or scary or capable of ending the world to be successful. Be familiar with the current site standards and what the community is expecting in an article of quality.
  • Be aware of forum activity!
    • If you're not inclined to write a thorough review (i.e., covering concept, execution, a few examples of specific fixes, and so on), please hold off on making the first post so a more experienced reviewer can address the thread first. That gives the author a more accurate gauge of the potential overall audience response.

For some reading to get the creativity engine running, consider:

  • http://www.scp-wiki.net/essays-on-style (a bunch of authors talk about how/where they get their ideas!)
  • http://www.scp-wiki.net/ideation (a bunch of different ways to explore ideas!)
  • http://www.scp-wiki.net/things-what-do-a-thing-an-essay-on-things (a bunch of ways to handle the classic "thing that does a thing" SCP formula!)

We've also got the Reviewers' Spotlight, which shows off great pieces picked by prominent reviewers for front-page fame!

Remember, reviewers can shape a concept from "meh" to "holy #%$@!!" You speak for a portion of the audience when you respond to an author, and play a key role in the development of the site's material and canon. Best of luck with all your reviewing endeavors!
